What is VSI?
VSI (Virtual Source Installer) is an app that lets you install multiple APKs as if it was a single package. This is useful for installing apps that are distributed as App Bundles since Android provides no built-in way to install them from sources other than Google Play.

How to use VSI?
Click "Install APKs" button and select base APK and additional configuration-specific APKs or a ZIP archive that contains all required APKs, then click "Select" button to start installation process.

.apks
You can rename a .zip archive that contains .apk files to .apks (e.g.: somesplitapp.zip -> somesplitapp.apks), so it can be opened with VSI from other apps.

Installing apps from external storage
You can long click install button to select files via system file picker that supports external storage.

Seriously, read this one-time warning!

Sorry for taking your time, but I'm really tired of people with MIUI who have been skipping the previous version of this warning.

Looks like your device is running MIUI. MIUI is known for breaking standard Android API features and a lot of VSI users have reported installations failing on MIUI for no reason with "Installation failed". Usually it can be fixed by disabling MIUI optimizations in developer settings, which I suggest you should do.

Of course you can try using VSI without disabling MIUI optimization, but if it doesn't work, try disabling it before complaining to me about failed installations. If your MIUI version doesn't have that toggle or it doesn't help, there's nothing I can do.

This issue is supposed to be fixed on MIUI 20.2.20 and up (xiaomi.eu and eu-based ROMs).

Backup of %d apps has been cancelled

Managed backups are currently in beta, please report issues in VSI's GitHub repo (you can find the link on about screen)

Backup files format
VSI backups apps as .apks files (which are just ZIP archives with .apk files) with some meta information added to the archive (such as app name and icon). Backed up .apks files can still be installed as normal .apks files (because they are normal .apks files, except for some additional files in the archive which are ignored by installer)

What is backed up
Currently VSI backups only apps APK files (no data/obb/etc)

External changes to backup directory
VSI doesn't automatically keep track of external changes done to files in the backup directory. So, if you've changed them outside of VSI, use reindex option in 3-dots menu at the top right of backup screen to rescan backups directory.

VSI System Installer integration for LSPosed and Vector
LSPosed / Vector · Redirect Android’s stock APK installer into VSI without replacing the system app.

VSI includes an Xposed-compatible system installer hook. Enable VSI as a module in LSPosed or Vector and scope it only to com.google.android.packageinstaller. Direct APK VIEW / INSTALL_PACKAGE launches are then redirected into VSI. Android PackageInstaller confirmation flows remain stock to prevent rootless install loops. Disable the module, remove it from scope, remove Vector/LSPosed, or reboot after temporary root and the original system installer works normally again. No system APK is modified.
